why: This is the two-step sign-in gate. readSession() is changed to skip the Supabase Auth call when the mirror is empty, and admit() is changed to reconcile the mirror and to sign out when Auth is unreachable. The code described matches auth.ts (the getUser block, the mirror writes at two-step.ts 190/264/341/362). A small slip in the condition, such as skipping when two_step_reenrol_at is set, or letting an Auth error leave enrolled false, lets an account with a factor in at aal1. The int cases cover the listed flows, but a reviewer must read the gate itself. Commit 2 also leaves an open-ended option: do code-review FF4 (cart and checkout reads in one Promise.all) 'only if it is small'.
harm_if_wrong: An attacker with only a password would get into the admin of an account that has two-step on, which is a security hole in production.
brief_problems: The migration body as written is not valid SQL. The notice text has no quotes ('raise notice two-step mirror reconcile skipped: ...') and the block ends 'end $;' instead of 'end $$;'. 'Single quotes as SQL needs them' leaves the executor to repair it.

Commit 2 lets the executor optionally change cart and checkout loaders for code-review row 3.8 (FF4) 'if it is small'. That is a judgement on the checkout path that this step otherwise does not touch. Drop it and leave the row's note as 'FF4 open'.
Commit 2 says to use afterAnswer() 'if it does exactly this', and to add an exported readSessionNow 'if the test only reaches the React-cached readSession'. Both are small conditional design choices.
